overview: Unlike the OV7670's raw parallel bus, the Raspberry Pi Camera Module connects over a dedicated CSI ribbon cable straight into the Pi's own image signal processor, which handles all the low-level capture work in hardware. The result is a plug-and-play experience from the software side: a couple of lines of Python (via libcamera/picamera2) and you're capturing photos or video, with the Pi's GPU doing the heavy lifting of encoding. It only works with Raspberry Pi boards specifically — the CSI connector and protocol aren't a generic standard other microcontrollers can use.
simpleSummary: A camera made specifically for the Raspberry Pi, plugging straight into its dedicated camera port.

specifications.interface: CSI (Camera Serial Interface) ribbon cable — Raspberry Pi only
specifications.video: Up to 4K on newer modules, 1080p common baseline
specifications.powerSource: Powered through the CSI ribbon cable itself, no separate power wiring
specifications.focusType: Fixed-focus or autofocus depending on module version

pinMap.name: CSI Connector
pinMap.function: The entire interface is a single 15/22-pin CSI ribbon cable carrying power, clock, and high-speed differential data lanes to the Pi's dedicated camera port.
pinMap.voltageRange: N/A (ribbon cable interface, not individual pins)
pinMap.gotcha: Must be inserted the correct way around (contacts facing the right direction) into both the camera and the Pi's CSI port, or nothing will be detected — a very common first-time setup mistake.

useCases.title: Computer vision robot
useCases.scenario: Feed live video into OpenCV or a TensorFlow Lite model running on the Pi for object detection/tracking.

useCases.title: Time-lapse / security camera
useCases.scenario: Simple scheduled or motion-triggered photo/video capture project.

useCases.title: Video calling / streaming appliance
useCases.scenario: Combine with a Pi and network connection for a DIY streaming camera.

oftenConfusedWith: USB webcams (work on any computer, not just a Pi, but with more USB/CPU overhead)
oftenUpgradedTo: Raspberry Pi HQ Camera (interchangeable lenses, larger sensor)
